consumer_contexts: games shipped on several headset platforms that keep a persistent managers set loaded and move the person between a menu set and content sets through a fade, a loading state, and a fade back, and must recover to a safe set when a load fails

training, showcase, and installation XR applications that switch between authored environments on an operator's or a person's request, need every transition to be replayable for review, and must never leave the headset on a frozen or black view
common_kernel: scene set and scene identities as validated closed identities separate from any scene asset, path, build index, or addressable key
a declared scene graph of sets, member scenes, exactly one active scene per set, and one fallback set, validated fail-closed at construction

load, unload, and switch intents applied to an immutable flow state through a transition state machine (idle, fading out, loading, holding, fading in) with typed fade and hold durations and stable failure codes
error recovery in which a failed load records load.failed and transitions to the declared fallback set
deterministic replay of an intent sequence, including elapsed-time and load-completion intents, to an equal state and fingerprint
configurable_variation: the fade-out, hold, and fade-in durations, the fallback set, and which sets a product declares
adapter-side binding of scene ids to build-list scenes or, in a separately validated sibling adapter, to addressable keys, and the fade surface implementation
consumer-owned loading-screen content, fade art, persistent managers, and what is restored after a switch
excluded_project_specific: one product's scene list, level order, loading-screen art, fade colour, and menu structure
one project's save-and-restore behaviour across a switch, asset bundling, and platform store review outcome
rationale: Scene flow is a recurring cross-project need whose kernel (validated scene set identity, a declared graph with one active scene per set, additive load, unload, and switch intents through an explicit fade, load, hold, and fade-in sequence, recovery to a fallback set, and deterministic state) is shared by the engine's own scene-management, activation-hold, and scene-list documentation, a second engine subsystem's scene event lifecycle, three platform guidelines on loading states and transition comfort, and two independent open-source implementations, while every product keeps its own scene list, loading-screen content, fade art, and restore behaviour outside the shared Core.
non_claims: Admission does not claim load time, hitching, dropped frames, activation cost, memory behaviour, comfort during a transition, fade visibility, or any named-device behaviour; those require a Device Lab receipt.
Admission does not claim that the pinned editor exposes the build scene list through the page cited; a person confirms the current scene-list API before the adapter is planned.

This draft becomes a decision only when a maintainer copies it into docs/foundry/admissions/ after a person confirms the sources, page paths, versions, and the maintenance state of each open-source implementation.
